selected_gaps.gap: [additive] Q-WAM 与 SteerQuant 使用离线 calibration probes，QuantWAMs 用 FP16 reference-state replay 提议 schedule 并将 quantized-state profile 作为 shift diagnostic，PreDE 对新配置则查询固定 observation log；这些结果尚未确立当量化动作改变后续 observation history 时，离线分数/阈值对多轮闭环候选排序仍保持校准。Phase 2 的构造交付应是在固定 evaluator 与 W4A4/W4A8 条件下，提出能在候选诱发的新闭环 history 上维持量化质量判断的方法，并通过多轮 evidence 检验迁移；不预定状态适配机制。stakes: 实践者在长序列或接触状态变化时可能遇到离线通过、闭环退化的候选并付出额外仿真或实机成本；intellectual 上，固定输入 evidence 不能支持跨 rollout distribution 的控制保真结论。
selected_gaps.selection_rationale: 这是直接约束 WAM 低比特配置在多轮闭环部署中能否维持质量判断的 method gap，且 Phase 1 明确要求在固定 W4A4/W4A8 与 evaluator 下构造方法。self_supervised_signal_engineering 的模型自产生观察与输出信号可形成 quantizer calibration 目标，直接把候选自身访问到的 history 纳入 scale refit；普通 on-policy/DAgger 已是强基线，因此新颖性只按是否超过该基线判断。

phase2_select/phase2_select_output.json.deliverable_coverage: method — anchor gap → self_supervised_signal_engineering 使用量化 WAM 自身诱发的闭环 observations 更新 A8 activation clipping scales。

user_direction_disposition.user_wanted: 最好量化层级能到W4A4/W4A8，混合精度或者单一精度都可以
user_direction_disposition.chosen: 采用单一 W4A8 配置，固定 W4 权重量化并迭代校准 A8 激活 clipping scales。

phase2_select/phase2_select_output.json.composition_note: 单腿量化标定机制：由当前 W4A8 候选生成的新闭环 observations 提供校准输入，只更新既有 A8 clipping 参数；不加入 evaluation-only 组件。其定位是 WAM 低比特场景中的 application/incremental 迁移，若普通 on-policy DAgger 量化器校准已给出同等效果，则不主张算法新颖性。

deferred_gaps.gap: [subtractive] Q-WAM、SteerQuant、QuantWAMs 与 PreDE 都在完整 chunk 或固定 execution condition 下定义量化分数；尚无文献检验“完整生成 chunk 足以代表部署 fidelity”这一共享前提，在只执行某个 prefix 并经固定 controller 运算后是否仍成立。Phase 2 的构造交付应是在固定 controller 与 W4A4/W4A8 条件下，提出并检验能保留已执行 command 行为的量化方法，同时界定完整 chunk 分数何时会失真；不预定其内部机制。若高影响误差集中在首段或控制阈值附近，量化配置可能按未执行尾部误差排序而错过已执行 command 偏差；stakes: practitioner 在机器人部署时会接受错误配置并承担任务失败或重复闭环评估成本，intellectual 上会把 full-chunk similarity 错当成控制等价。
deferred_gaps.reason: 本候选把控制器与执行 prefix 固定为 rollout 条件，损失仍比较完整 action chunk；不会回答完整 chunk 分数与实际 controller-transformed prefix command 是否一致。

deferred_gaps.gap: [additive] 对同时发生于多个 layer、stream 与 denoising step 的低位误差，Q-WAM 明确省略交叉项并依赖零均值/不相关近似，SteerQuant 则以 full-precision 输入单独估计每个区域；因此在 W4A4/W4A8 联合量化时，边际分数是否能预测误差合成后的 action displacement 仍未知，尤其是系统偏移、抵消或同向累积是否改变候选排序。Phase 2 的构造交付应是在固定 WAM 与低位宽下，提出能应对多处残差同时存在的量化方法，并以联合扰动证据检验其 action 误差判断；不预定误差估计或调节机制。stakes: 量化研究者可能把精度预算分给单点敏感却在联合路径中不关键的模块，造成 W4 quality 结论不可复现或无法迁移到不同校准轨迹；intellectual 上会把独立扰动假设当成未经检验的误差几何。
deferred_gaps.reason: 本候选只在新 history 上重拟合激活 clipping scales，不估计或校正多个 layer/stream/denoising-step 量化残差的交叉项。

phase2_generate/phase2_generate_output.j.title: Quantized-History DAgger for WAM W4A8 Activation PTQ

intervention_object.acts_on: Fast-WAM denoiser per-(Linear layer, token stream, denoising step) A8 clipping limits alpha_{l,s,t}; W4 weight quantizers stay fixed.
intervention_object.operator: Refit only the A8 clipping limits using full action-chunk discrepancy between W4A8 and the same frozen BF16 WAM on observations visited by the current quantized closed loop.
intervention_object.decision_variables: alpha_{l,s,t} only; the layer set, stream/step indexing, W4 group scales, controller, replan schedule, and action execution prefix are fixed.

phase2_generate/phase2_generate_output.j.hook: The candidate is a W4A8 activation-PTQ calibration loop that uses the quantized WAM's own closed-loop observations to refit clipping scales. Its falsifiable prediction is that held-out full-chunk action discrepancy falls on quantized-history observations, with a smaller or absent gain on BF16-reference histories.
phase2_generate/phase2_generate_output.j.hook_shape_rationale: Shape (a): the named metric is held-out action-chunk discrepancy, and the predicted history-source interaction is non-obvious because QuantWAMs reports a quantized-state shift profile but does not use it to refit quantizer parameters. Shape (b) was plausible because fixed reference histories underlie prior calibration, but QuantWAMs explicitly acknowledges the distribution-shift limitation, so calling that assumption tacit would overstate the reframe.

gap_closure.sub_pattern_not_applicable_reason: C07's continuous label-free adaptation signal and C08's generate-filter-retrain loop each add requirements this quantizer-only on-policy calibration does not use; neither is a faithful sub-pattern fit.
gap_closure.how_closed: The current W4A8 WAM supplies its own newly visited observations, and the same frozen BF16 WAM supplies matched-seed action targets for refitting only the A8 clipping table. The parent pattern has no WAM-low-bit domain-adjacent sub-cluster example in the reviewed cards, so this is a parent-only, application/incremental fit.

phase2_generate/phase2_generate_output.j.core_mechanism: Apply the parent pattern at the calibration-signal level: the current W4A8 Fast-WAM policy generates observations through its own closed-loop interaction with the fixed LIBERO-Goal evaluator, so its visited-history distribution D_Q(phi) is the signal source rather than an FP16-only observation log. At each visited observation, run the quantized candidate and the same frozen BF16 checkpoint with matched denoising randomness and compare their complete action chunks; define L_act(phi;D_Q(phi)) as the expected squared difference after the checkpoint's existing per-action normalization. Refit only symmetric A8 clipping limits alpha_{l,s,t} for each quantized Linear layer, stream, and denoising step to reduce this loss; keep signed groupwise W4 weights and their zero-point-zero scales fixed. Re-run the quantized policy after each refit so the next calibration set reflects the newly induced history distribution; do not differentiate through the simulator or update WAM weights. At deployment, load the frozen clipping table and use the ordinary W4A8 GEMM path; the BF16 teacher is calibration-only and no precision schedule or controller setting changes. This is a DAgger-style quantizer-calibration application, not a new general PTQ algorithm, and neither success nor closed-loop stability nor speedup follows without separate evidence.
phase2_generate/phase2_generate_output.j.core_mechanism_reasoning:
BLOCK 1 — PREMISES ledger:
- A released Fast-WAM checkpoint can be run both in BF16 and under W4A8, and the fixed LIBERO-Goal simulator/evaluator can expose observations reached by the quantized policy; this is the named implementation setting in engineering_anchors.zh.md.
- Untested — falsification target: quantizer clipping scales fit on the candidate's own reachable observations reduce action-chunk discrepancy on later quantized-history observations beyond one-pass on-policy calibration.
- The update uses model-generated teacher outputs rather than environment action labels; teacher queries are made only during calibration, and their count/cost must be recorded.
- observation-model: draw initial episodes from the existing LIBERO-Goal calibration split and follow the fixed quantized policy, simulator, controller, and replanning schedule; D_Q(phi) is the distribution of observations actually reached before each episode terminates. Terminal/failure states censor later observations, so the estimand is conditional on reachable visits under this evaluator, not on unobserved counterfactual states.
- ESTIMAND: R_act(phi;D_Q(phi)) = E_{o~D_Q(phi),xi}[||D_a^{-1}(a_phi(o,xi)-a_BF16(o,xi))||_2^2], where xi is matched denoising randomness, D_a is the checkpoint's existing action-normalization vector, and both models receive the same observation o; this is full-action behavior fidelity on quantized-induced histories, not task success or executed-command fidelity.

BLOCK 2 — NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT: the naive version is one-pass on-policy DAgger quantizer calibration: collect observations visited by W4A8, query the BF16 teacher on those observations, and refit alpha once with the same action loss. There is no reason this baseline must fail, and ordinary DAgger may already solve the distribution mismatch; therefore the proposal is explicitly application/incremental, with no new-algorithm claim unless refreshed quantized-history refits beat one-pass DAgger and generic adversarial PTQ under matched W4A8 coverage.

BLOCK 3 — DESIGN RATIONALE: one method leg is sufficient because the anchor gap is the transfer of a quantizer quality signal across candidate-induced histories; adding a diagnostic sibling would only measure that mechanism. Reusing QuantWAMs' fixed-intervention profile alone was rejected because its paper treats the quantized-state profile as a shift diagnostic and derives its protection schedule from FP16 replay, while PreDE screens on fixed observations without changing the quantizer. We keep controller, action prefix, precision allocation, and WAM weights fixed so any change comes from refitting activation clipping on the candidate's visited states.
phase2_generate/phase2_generate_output.j.core_mechanism_steps:
1. Freeze one released Fast-WAM checkpoint, inference mode, observation preprocessing, denoising schedule, LIBERO-Goal evaluator, controller, execution prefix, and calibration/development/test episode splits.
2. Quantize every denoiser Linear projection (joint-attention Q/K/V/O, FFN/MoE, conditioning/AdaLN, and action projections) to signed groupwise W4 weights with zero point 0 and signed symmetric A8 activations with zero point 0. Keep W4 group scales fixed; define one A8 clipping limit alpha_{l,s,t} per target layer, stream, and denoising step.
3. Initialize alpha from ordinary static PTQ calibration on the available reference-policy histories, producing the W4A8 starting candidate; do not update any WAM weights.
4. Run that candidate closed-loop on the calibration episodes under the frozen evaluator and record every pre-replan observation, model history/cache needed for inference, executed action history, and denoising seed. The environment produces D_Q(phi); controller and replanning rules remain unchanged.
5. At each recorded observation, replay the candidate and BF16 checkpoint with matched denoising randomness, compare the full generated action chunks after the checkpoint's existing action normalization, and accumulate L_act(phi;D_Q(phi)).
6. Update only alpha_{l,s,t} by minimizing the mean L_act on the collected Q-history observations; W4 weight scales, model parameters, bit allocation, and controller stay fixed. Re-run the quantized policy to refresh D_Q after each update, stopping when held-out action discrepancy ceases to improve or the preregistered pilot compute budget B is reached.
7. Freeze the final W4A8 quantizer and evaluate it without BF16 teacher calls on separate LIBERO-Goal episodes; report action discrepancy on its own visited histories and closed-loop success as separate outcomes. No native speed claim is made until a WAM-compatible packed W4A8 kernel is measured.
phase2_generate/phase2_generate_output.j.falsification_prediction: Use one released Fast-WAM checkpoint and LIBERO-Goal with the same inference mode, initial episodes, controller, execution prefix, replanning schedule, denoising seeds, and W4A8 Linear coverage; compare static reference-history PTQ, one-pass on-policy/DAgger quantizer calibration, multi-round self-induced-history refitting, and generic adversarial PTQ. The primary metric is held-out R_act on observations generated by each frozen quantized candidate's own rollouts; if the mechanism helps, this full-action discrepancy decreases for multi-round refitting, while closed-loop success is reported separately and no task-success inference is drawn from R_act. The load-bearing variable is g_Qhist = the gradient of L_act with respect to alpha estimated on observations from the current candidate's own quantized rollouts; as a negative control, replace g_Qhist with the same gradient estimated from matched BF16-reference-policy histories, which should raise held-out Q-history R_act toward the one-pass/PTQ baseline. If multi-round updates do not improve over one-pass DAgger or generic adversarial PTQ, record the recipe as incremental/no-go and stop rather than widening the campaign.
phase2_generate/phase2_generate_output.j.compute_budget: Suggested pilot: about 2–4 GPU-days on one 80GB-class GPU for one Fast-WAM checkpoint, calibration rollouts, BF16 teacher queries on visited states, and held-out LIBERO-Goal evaluation; no paid API cost. This excludes substantial native W4A8 kernel porting and is an estimate, not measured runtime.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: Q-WAM estimates AOG from randomized probes and routes selected directions through a 16-bit ASP branch, whereas this candidate adds no high-precision branch and refits only A8 clipping limits using observations reached by the quantized closed loop.

SteerQuant's action-impact map is computed on full-precision inputs and remains fixed during calibration; this candidate instead uses current W4A8-induced observations as the data distribution for updating activation clipping limits.

QuantWAMs uses quantized-state profiles to diagnose distribution shift but proposes its fixed-budget protection schedule from FP16 reference replay; this candidate consumes quantized-policy histories to refit the quantizer's A8 scales themselves.

PreDE predicts whether a new configuration is acceptable from a fixed observation log, while this candidate changes the configuration's activation clipping limits using the candidate's own visited observations and frozen-teacher outputs.

phase2_generate/phase2_generate_output.j.what_step_was_missed: QuantWAMs would have needed to close its reported distribution-shift diagnostic loop by optimizing quantizer parameters on observations generated by the current quantized policy, then rerunning that updated quantizer to refresh its own induced history distribution; its paper instead uses the quantized profile for diagnosis while deriving the protected-step schedule from FP16 reference-state replay.
